messages:
IncidentBot: Pager alert SEV1 - model-shard-read-errors > 15% for s3-backed shard-store (ap-south1 / us-west2). Auto-escalate flagged. (thread start)
Micah: I'm awake and looking. Confirming impact: model loads failing intermittently, causing cold-start 500s. Setting severity P1.
June: Oncall handover in 3. I'll own comms. Sam you free to help coordinate vendor contact?
Sam: On it. Pulling latest logs. Seeing repeated TCP resets to s3.amazonaws.com edge egress via our NAT gateway.
Tal: Infra quick check: our egress NAT in us-west2 shows high connection retries and 502s from managed LB. Kernel netstat shows TIME_WAIT spike.
Ravi: Any upstream advisories from AWS?
AWS Support Bot: Case opened: AWS-20260315-4432. Reported: High 5xx from S3 edge in us-west-2 affecting customers using our shared NAT IPs. Initial response: acknowledged, network team investigating.
Micah: Sam escalate to AWS account TAM and request bump to urgent, ask for ETA and mitigation path (alternate egress IPs or regional failover).
Sam: Message to TAM sent. Asked for dedicated routing or filtered IP-range. Requested conference bridge.
June: Drafting status page and customer email: short, transparent, explain vendor network issue affecting model loads for some regions; provide mitigation steps and timeframe. Will post update every 20m.
June: Internal comm template (for product/sales Slack banner): "Service disruption: model loads intermittently failing in select regions due to upstream cloud network error. See status.redwood.ai for updates. Support is handling prioritized customers." Feedback?
Micah: Add link to support ticket and note affected endpoints / guidance for retries.
Tal: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Enable aggressive local artifact caching on inference nodes to avoid S3 fetch on cold-starts, 2) Shift new model loads to us-east-1 and ap-southeast-1 via routing rule, 3) Temporarily enlarge model warm pool to reduce cold starts.
Sam: Rolling cache-mode=aggressive to us-west2 now.
IncidentBot: Feature flag rollout to cache-mode=aggressive at 02:05Z -> 10% nodes.
Tal: Canary nodes show cold-start errors dropped by 70%. Scaling warm pool now (api call: POST /admin/warm-pool/adjust {region: "us-west-2", count: 50}).
AWS Support Bot: Update from AWS: network team identified routing instability at a shared egress cluster; they applied a mitigation at 02:24Z but recommend customers implement failover for critical workloads. ETA for full remediation unknown.
Ravi: For Dedicated customers with direct peering, check if they saw impact. Notifying SAs to escalate any customer complaining.
June: Posted status page update 02:30Z: "Partial mitigation in place; artifact caching reduces errors for many customers; working with AWS on full fix. Next update in 20m." Sent targeted emails to top 5 impacted customers with steps and support contact.
Micah: Need vendor comms playbook: pre-approved entitlements for escalation, TAM escalation list, and legal contact if SLAs impacted. Ravi take ownership.
Ravi: Acknowledged. Will collect TAM contacts, create prioritized phone tree, and propose pre-authorization scope for vendor actions in emergencies.
Sam: AWS requested logs and traceroutes; they opened a conference bridge at 02:42Z. On the bridge now with their network eng.
Tal: While on bridge, we tested failover to us-east-1 and ap-south-1. us-east-1 traffic handled model loads normally. Implemented emergency routing policy to prefer regions with healthy egress.
IncidentBot: Routing rollout success to 60% of new model load requests at 02:49Z.
June: Customer comms update 02:55Z: "We have rerouted new model loads to alternate regions and increased caching to minimize cold-starts. AWS applied a temporary network mitigation. We will follow up with root cause once confirmed." Sent to impacted customers.
AWS Support Bot: AWS network update 03:05Z: temporary mitigation holding; full root cause investigation ongoing. Suggested customers implement multi-region artifact replication to mitigate future correlated egress problems.
Micah: Action items before incident close: 1) Short-term: add egress health monitors + automatic multi-region failover rule, 2) Medium: pre-replicate critical artifact sets to at least two regions, 3) Long-term: vendor escalation runbook + pre-approved TAM contact list + legal escalation threshold. Assign owners: Tal, Sam, Ravi.
June: I'll formalize the status and email templates we used and add a vendor-escalation checklist for comms.
Sam: AWS confirmed case number AWS-20260315-4432 will remain open. They will provide a timeline and RCA. Pushing for expedited RCA for our postmortem.
Micah: We're stabilizing; errors down to 2% from 18% at peak. Keep monitoring for one hour before declaring resolved.
IncidentBot: Incident marked resolved at 03:22Z after metrics stable for 30m.
Micah: Assigning postmortem: Sam (vendor coordination), Tal (mitigations & infra follow-ups), June (comm templates), Ravi (escalation playbook). Please create follow-up tasks and link to incident doc.
June: Creating post-incident comms pack and internal note for Sales/Support.
Micah: Thanks everyone. Reminder: add multi-region artifact replication to our Optimize roadmap and prioritize pre-approved vendor escalation contacts in the oncall runbook. End of thread.
